question: An events manager is preparing an attendee FAQ. She has last year's FAQ, the signed contract for this year's venue, and an email thread with the caterer. What should she do first?
options: A) Ask Claude to draft the FAQ from last year's version, then check it against the contract and the caterer emails.
B) Paste all three documents together and ask Claude to work out which of the details in them are the most current ones.
C) Summarise each of the three documents on her own, and paste only those summaries so the request stays compact.
D) Decide which document is authoritative this year, and label each as she pastes it so Claude knows which one wins.
correct_answers: D) Decide which document is authoritative this year, and label each as she pastes it so Claude knows which one wins.
explanations: Drafting from the superseded document first anchors the FAQ on last year's arrangements, and checking afterwards catches only the differences she happens to look for.
Nothing in the documents states which is newest or which governs, so this hands a decision she alone can make to a source that cannot see the contractual hierarchy.
Her own summaries drop the specifics attendees ask about, such as exact times and access rules, and the precedence problem is still unresolved.

Correct. The three sources disagree by design: the contract supersedes last year's FAQ, and the email thread may supersede both on catering. Establishing precedence and labelling each source is what stops last year's details being presented as this year's.
